Items.Authors: Youming Guo, Lingxiao Li, Zibo Ke
Items.Title: Design and implementation of a 4.2-m telescope adaptive optics system for solar system object observations and laser guide star performance testing
Items.Abstract: A spatiotemporal reference frame underpins human activity and science. The 4.2-m ground-based astrometric telescope will maintain high-precision Solar System ephemerides by tracking the orbits of planets, dwarf planets, satellites, and asteroids for space missions. Atmospheric turbulence limits large apertures, so adaptive optics (AO) is required for high resolution. To enable both narrow- and wide-field observing, we will develop conventional AO for near diffraction-limited imaging in narrow fields and ground-layer AO (GLAO) for wide fields. GLAO targets dominant near-ground turbulence: multiple sodium laser guide stars sample different directions and drive ground-layer wavefront correction, improving seeing over a larger field. A deformable secondary mirror will simplify the system, reduce residual wavefront error, and increase throughput and sky coverage. R&D covers sodium beacon lasers, multi-LGS wavefront sensing, high-density deformable secondaries, and wavefront control overall

Items.Authors: Thomas Schweizer, Josef Eder, Holger Wetteskind, Christopher Jablonski, Robert Stadler, Masahiro Teshima, Razmik Mirzoyan, Armand Fiasson, Nicolas Geffroy, Guillaume Deleglise, Oscar Blanch, Julia Mundet, Rafael Garcia, Antonio Jose Penuela Lopez
Items.Title: Design and realisation of the 23m diameter LST mechanical structure for the Cherenkov Telescope Array
Items.Abstract: The 23 m diameter Large Size Cherenkov Telescope for CTA, located at 2250 m a.s.l. on the Canary Island of La  Palma, is the next-generation Cherenkov telescope following MAGIC, H.E.S.S., and VERITAS. To enable rapid  repositioning (180° in 18 s) for gamma-ray burst observations, the mechanical structure was designed to be ultra-  lightweight (110 tons). The space-frame structure consists of slender struts made of carbon fibre, aluminium and steel. The telescope is designed to withstand extreme environmental conditions at the ORM observatory on La Palma, including wind speeds up to 200 km/h, uplift forces, and ice loads of up to 30 tons. We present the structural design developed to meet these functional and environmental requirements. MPP Munich is responsible for the telescope's mechanical structure together with partner institutes in France (LAPP) and Spain (IFAE). The prototype, LST-1, has been operational since 2019, and three additional LSTs are currently under construction.

Items.Authors: Shi-hao Lu, Hong-fei Zhang, Hao-ran Ma, Qiang Wu, Yong Yang, Jian Wang, Hai-feng Xu
Items.Title: Design of a compact scientific CCD camera with EMI suppression
Items.Abstract: The requisite vacuum and cryogenic environments for optimal scientific-grade Charge Coupled Device (CCD) operation have posed significant challenges to its miniaturization. This paper presents the design of a compact, scientific-grade CCD camera utilizing a CCD47-20 sensor and a Thermoelectric Cooler (TEC). The design achieves a balance between a small form factor and low readout noise, incorporating an analog baseline restoration circuit. This design consists of a front-amplifier board, a power supply board, a driver board, and a main control board. Furthermore, a separate TEC driver board with electromagnetic interference (EMI) suppression is implemented to minimize interference from the cooling process on the CCD signal. Test results demonstrate that the system achieves excellent performance, validating the effectiveness of the design.

Items.Authors: Zhimin Ren, Haikun Wen, Wenyuan Wang, Zhengyang Li
Items.Title: Design of a flexible lifting fixture and parametric optimization of lifting points for large precision optical glass
Items.Abstract: Large precision optical mirrors in astronomical telescopes require safe and precise handling. This paper presents a flexible nine-point Whiffletree lifting system for mirrors with diameters ≥4 m. The system comprises a main steel frame and three flexible support arms connected via universal joints, providing six degrees of freedom to achieve uniform load distribution. Lifting claws feature rotational endpoints, with some driven by remote-controlled motors to avoid interference with mirror support points. Limit devices on the frame and internal guide rollers ensure accurate alignment. The design, on-site assembly, and empty-load verification are detailed. The system is lightweight, supports large loads, and ensures balanced forces, offering a reliable and efficient solution for handling and installing large optical mirrors.

Items.Authors: Shuo Wang, Qihang Zhang, Ping Zhang, Chao Zhai
Items.Title: Design of a next-generation fiber optic positioning unit drive system
Items.Abstract: In order to advance the LAMOST Phase II project, this paper aims to design a motor drive system based on STM32. First, a PCB drive board with a simpler structure and richer functionality was designed using Cadence Allegro, and components were reselected. Second, based on the Keil development software, a rigorous communication program was designed according to the instructions from the host computer, including processes such as data frame transmission and reception handling, two-step operation, and error feedback mechanisms. At the same time, a new drive program was redesigned, utilizing an 'S-shaped' acceleration and deceleration curve for smooth start and stop, allowing the motor to start and stop at any phase, and replacing full-step driving with microstepping. Experimental results show that the drive board has a compact structure and complete functions; the software program can meet the expected requirements.

Items.Authors: Kosuke Kushibiki, Shinobu Ozaki, Toshihiro Tsuzuki, Yutaka Yamagata, Takuya Hosobata, Masahiro Takeda, Shinya Morita, Keiichi Nakagawa, Yuki Inada, Kentaro Motohara, Hidenori Takahashi, Masahiro Konishi, Natsuko Kato, Jeung Yun, Akino Yasuda, Tomoya Yukino, Misato Fujii, Kensho Tanaka, Taiki Kikuchi
Items.Title: Design of an image-slicer integral field unit with free-form mirrors for a near-infrared spectrograph SWIMS
Items.Abstract: SWIMS-IFU is an image-slicer-type integral field unit (IFU) for a near-infrared imager and spectrograph SWIMS, one of the first-generation instruments for the TAO 6.5 m telescope. By optimizing a slice width to a typical seeing of 0.5″, SWIMS-IFU provides a wider field of view (FoV) of 17.17″ x 14.0″ compared with existing near-infrared integral field spectrographs.    Due to the limited volume of 235 mm x 170 mm x 55 mm allowed for the IFU, it turns out to be impossible to design an optical system using ordinary spherical mirrors without introducing significant aberrations. To overcome this issue, we have designed an optical system using multiple free-form mirrors. This design delivers nearly diffraction-limited performance at the image slicer. The complex mirror geometries will be realized using an ultra-precision cutting technique.    In this presentation, we will describe the specifications and details of the SWIMS-IFU optical design.

Items.Authors: Jie Hu, Zheng Lou, Wei Geng, Qiang Zhi, Zhi Li, Yutan Zhang, Jiameng Wang, Zhenhui Lin, Zheng Wang, Kangmin Zhou, Jing Li, Shengcai Shi
Items.Title: Design of multicolor large field of view camera for XSMT based on kinetic inductance detectors
Items.Abstract: In this presentation, we introduce the design of a wide-field kinetic inductance detector (KID) camera currently being developed for the 15-m XSMT telescope, which is under construction at XueShanMuChang, Qinghai, China (96°35′08.6″ E, 37°58′36.2″ N; altitude 4,820 m). The instrument provides a 14′ field of view, has an effective focal ratio of f/2.9, and operates simultaneously in three frequency bands centered at 230, 345, and 460 GHz. The camera will be deployed in two stages, primarily driven by the size of the cryostat. In the first stage, the instrument will include the 345 and 460 GHz bands. In the second stage, the 345 and 460 GHz bands will be integrated into a single focal plane, and the 230 GHz band will be added. The current design focuses on the 345 and 460 GHz bands. The focal plane has a diameter of 190 mm and accommodates seven horn-coupled lumped-element KID arrays using Hilbert-curve meanders. In total, the camera contains approximately 8,000 pixels.

Items.Authors: Juriy Hastanin, Emmanuel Mazy, Alexandra Mazzoli, Colin Dandumont, Jean-Yves Plesseria, Laurence Rossi, Jean-François Vandenrijt, Marc P. Georges, Riccardo Gabrieli, Beatrice Tofani, Benedetta Talone
Items.Title: Design optimization of the forward baffle of the ESA Vigil heliospheric imager
Items.Abstract: Vigil is an upcoming ESA satellite mission designed to monitor space weather, with a particular focus on the solar corona and the interplanetary space between the Sun and Earth.  This paper introduces the basic design of a Forward Baffle (FB), currently being developed for the Heliospheric Imager (HI) instrument included in the Vigil spacecraft’s payload to observe very faint coronal mass ejections (CME) across a wide field of view.  The wide-angle FB is one of the key optical components of the HI designed to suppress direct stray-light from the solar disk. It consists of a multi-stage diffractive vanes (MSDV) module involving a pyramidal wedge structure with a high-reflectivity surface coating and a dedicated thermo-mechanically stabilized FB supporting assembly providing the required spatial and angular position of the MSDV relative to two observation cameras of the HI instrument. The FB supporting assembly is designed to meet the accommodation constrains of the HI instrument.

Items.Authors: Carlos Miravet, Jorge Mugica, Gonzalo Taubmann, Eneko Reina, Janire Zabaleta, Isabel Soto
Items.Title: Design, assembly, and test of a Sun polychromator prototype for TRUTHS mission
Items.Abstract: The TRUTHS mission, led by ESA, aims to establish a reference standard for Earth’s radiative state, enabling SI-traceable calibration and improving climate data consistency. A key element of its On-Board Calibration System is the Solar Polychromator (SPC), a tuneable bandpass instrument that filters solar radiation across 320–2400 nm for high-accuracy spectral calibration. This work presents the design and verification of a prototype SPC, developed to validate the optical concept before flight implementation. Laboratory tests using a monochromator assessed wavelength accuracy, spectral resolution (FWHM), and straylight suppression. Results show strong agreement between measured and predicted filtering behaviour, confirming accurate modelling and alignment. A Structural-Thermal-Optical Performance (STOP) analysis demonstrated stability under orbital thermal conditions.

Items.Authors: A. Orlati, A. Scalambra, M. Fiorentini, M. Poloni, F. Perini, A. Ladu, L. Schirru
Items.Title: Design, implementation, and test of the intermediate frequency distribution system for the Sardinia Radio Telescope high-frequency multifeed receivers
Items.Abstract: This paper presents the design and implementation of the new Intermediate Frequency Distribution (IFD) system for the Sardinia Radio Telescope (SRT). Developed for the telescope's upgrade to high-frequency bands, the IFD handles unprecedented bandwidths up to 18 GHz and high channel counts from new multi-feed receivers. The system ensures efficient signal routing from the receiver cabin to the digital backends in the control room. We detail the technical specifications derived from operational use cases and the custom architecture designed to integrate with the existing infrastructure. The study focuses on the technological solutions adopted for critical subsystems and presents comprehensive laboratory test results, demonstrating the system's essential role in enabling SRT’s advanced high-frequency capabilities.

Items.Authors: Jin Xin Jesse Lin, Keith Vanderlinde
Items.Title: Design, systems integration and validation of focus electronics for the Canadian Hydrogen Observatory and Radio-transient Detector
Items.Abstract: Large-N radio arrays, featuring hundreds or thousands of receivers, require precise alignment while presenting problems of reproducibility, cost, and systems integration. In response, we aim for a repeatable, low-cost, and highly manufacturable design of focus electronics for the Canadian Hydrogen Observatory and Radio-Transient Detector (CHORD). This is achieved through a combination of laser cutting, machining, injection moulding and FDM 3D printing. Additionally, metrology on all components is completed to verify manufacturing consistency. In this paper, I will discuss the design decisions of the focus electronics and systems integration with the full CHORD receiver chain.

Items.Authors: H. Hope Head, David Morris, Nuria Wright-Garba, Anthony Santini, Andres Parraguez, Alexandra Tritschler, David Boboltz
Items.Title: Designing a document management tool in JIRA for science operations specialists
Items.Abstract: The Science Operations Specialists at the National Science Foundation’s Daniel K. Inouye Solar Telescope developed an innovative use of Atlassian’s JIRA software as a documentation management tool. The primary objectives for creating this tool were to enhance team accessibility to the documentation workflow process, develop automation to ease the administrative and management task load, and enable supervisors to monitor documentation tasks in an optimized format. The team implemented this management system for both the procedural documentation involved with telescope operations as well as the knowledgebase and key concepts training documentation used in training new hires. Our overall documentation management system used Confluence as our documentation container and JIRA as our documentation process management and monitoring system. A predecessor Google Sheets tool defined the necessary content and provided a baseline for defining successful implementation within the JIRA space.

Items.Authors: Robin Anthony-Petersen, Steven E. Boggs, Emily Broadbent, Julian Gerber, Felix Hagemann, Sophia E. Haight, Dieter Hartmann, Carolyn A. Kierans, Matthew Lassiter, Alex Lowell, Brent Mochizuki, Samer Al Nussirat, Jarred Roberts, Parshad Patel, Nicole Rodriguez Cavero, Field Rogers, Clio C. Sleator, John A. Tomsick, Andreas Zoglauer
Items.Title: Detector-level calibrations for the COSI mission
Items.Abstract: Have you heard of the MeV gap? It’s the energy range between 0.1 and 30 MeV where our observing sensitivity is far lower than neighboring bands, yet where many extreme astrophysical phenomena can be studied. The Compton Spectrometer and Imager (COSI), a NASA Small Explorer mission launching in 2027, will observe the entire sky daily from 0.2–5 MeV with unprecedented sensitivity and excellent energy resolution (~0.5–1.2% FWHM), opening a new window into the soft gamma-ray sky. COSI’s main instrument consists of sixteen cross-strip high-purity germanium detectors. After fabrication, each detector undergoes extensive performance tests and detailed calibrations. Here we give an overview of COSI’s detectors, the testing setup, and the calibration efforts, which includes: energy, position, and timing calibration; studies of charge trapping and transport effects; measurements of detector deadtime; and the backend analysis pipeline.

Items.Authors: Lorenzo Merli, Luca Cortese, Daniele Vassallo, Oleksandra Rebrysh, Guido Agapito, Alfio Puglisi, Fabio Rossi, Alessandro Ballone, Simone Di Filippo, Valentina Viotto, Luca Marafatto, Carmelo Arcidiacono, Davide Greggio, Kalyan Radhakrishnan, Maria Bergomi
Items.Title: Developing a SPECULA-based digital twin for the MATTO test bench
Items.Abstract: MATTO (Multi-conjugate Adaptive Techniques Test Optics) is a wide field adaptive optics (AO) test bench currently under development at the INAF Astronomical Observatory of Padova. Its primary goal is to support the study and development of future multi-conjugate adaptive optics (MCAO) techniques.  The highly modular architecture enables MATTO to reproduce a broad variety of atmospheric conditions, optical configuration, and control strategies.  To validate the system’s design and support its calibration and performance optimization, we are developing a realistic numerical simulation to serve as a digital twin of the bench. The simulation is being built using SPECULA, a Python-based adaptive optics simulation package developed at INAF–Arcetri.  In this contribution, we present the first step toward MATTO digital twin implementation starting from the simulation of a scaled-down setup called MiniMATTO.

Items.Authors: Kian Syaifoel, Himadri Saha, Felix Münning, Matthias Justen, Netty Honingh, Jochem Baselmans, Dominik Riechers
Items.Title: Development and characterization of fabrication methods and materials for an MKID filterbank spectrometer
Items.Abstract: We are developing an on-chip filterbank spectrometer with the aim of performing line-intensity mapping of [CII] with the CCAT/FYST telescope. We target the 220 GHz - 440 GHz band, with a spectral resolution of R ~ 100. We present the progress towards kinetic inductance measurements of our sputtered Al films, which are needed for the design of our MKIDs. We also present our progress in fabrication methods, including a double-resist liftoff method in which we locally control the resist thickness and undercut. We furthermore look into the surface and interface treatments of our samples, in particular with respect to the quality of the NbTiN-Al interface and the sources of TLS noise.

Items.Authors: Fabienne Mangelsdorff, Andreas Stoll, Kalaga Madhav, Martin M. Roth, Lars Zimmermann, Stefan Lischke, Riya Mary Pattery
Items.Title: Development concept for a compact arrayed waveguide stacked multiobject spectrograph (CAWSMOS)
Items.Abstract: The linear size of a bulk optical astronomical spectrograph scales with the diameter of the primary mirror of the corresponding telescope. As modern telescopes continue to increase in aperture size, miniaturization of the spectrograph becomes crucial beyond the offered advantages in terms of multifunctional integration and photon efficiency.  The presented concept of development for a Compact Arrayed Waveguide Stacked Multi-Object Spectrograph (CAWSMOS) includes the design of the AWG chips, the stacking frame and cross-dispersion optics for the imaging of multiple spectral orders per AWG.  It aims to reduce the cost and size of astronomical spectrographs while also improving efficiency. This will bring the AWG technology closer to the realization of its full potential for ground based, airborne and spaceborne astronomical applications.

Items.Authors: Shogo Nohara, Kotaro Niinuma, Sogo Dan, Ayato Omori, Akira Kameyama, Kazuma Mukai, Hideo Ogawa, Naoto Sekiya, Pang Yuhong, Keita Sakuma, Yasumasa Yamasaki, Kei Amada, Kazuyoshi Sunada, Takuya Akahori, Tomoaki Oyama, Yutaka Hasegawa, Kohei Kurahara
Items.Title: Development of 6–18GHz wideband cooled receiver for VERA
Items.Abstract: VLBI Exploration of Radio Astrometry (VERA) network has been attracting attention on follow-up observations of transient phenomenon. To understand the radiation mechanism of non-thermal emission from such transient phenomena, simultaneous wide-band observation at centimeter wavelengths is essential. The Cassegrain design of VERA demands a large feed horn for the centimeter band, requiring a single broadband receiver. Furthermore, the centimeter band is heavily impacted by radio frequency interference (RFI) from satellite transmission and industrial use.   Therefore, we are developing a 6 – 18 GHz receiver featuring, (1) insertion of a low-loss High-Temperature Superconductivity Filter before the first amplifier to selectively cut RFI, (2) adoption of a 6 – 18 GHz Quadruple-Ridged Horn Antenna, and (3) use of a lightweight and compact Stirling Cryocooler.   In this poster, we will report on the design and status of the cooling dewar and the development progress of the receiving system.

Items.Authors: Tomonori Ikeda, Tatsuya Sawano, Naomi Tsuji, Yoshitaka Mizumura
Items.Title: Development of a gaseous electron-tracking Compton camera with electron-recoil reconstruction using deep learning
Items.Abstract: MeV gamma-ray observations remain far less explored than the X-ray, GeV, and TeV bands, creating the well-known MeV gap. A major challenge in this energy range is the improvement of the point spread function (PSF) of Compton telescopes. The electron-tracking Compton camera (ETCC) is one of the most promising instruments to overcome this gap, as its PSF strongly depends on the accuracy of the reconstructed electron-recoil direction. To address this, we developed a deep-learning–based reconstruction method using two-dimensional optical track images and one-dimensional waveform data. In simulations, the angular resolution for recoil electrons reached 44 degrees in the 40-50 keV range, surpassing our previous approach. This approach has the potential to enable the development of an optical-readout-based gaseous ETCC and to enhance the PSF of future MeV gamma-ray telescopes.

Items.Authors: Antonio Nazareno Uchoa de Oliveira Filho, Rafael Alves de Souza Ribeiro, Alex Cavaliéri Carciofi, Tiago Giorgetti
Items.Title: Development of a high-precision polarimetry roadmap at IAG-USP
Items.Abstract: We present the progress of a phased development program to build a high-precision polarimeter at IAG-USP, targeting sensitivities of $10^{-5}$ to $10^{-6}$ for small and medium-sized telescopes. The project addresses the instrumental gap in the Southern Hemisphere for polarimetric science, including exoplanet characterization and stellar magnetic fields. The proposed roadmap seeks to accelerate in-house instrumentation development at the IAG-USP Optics Laboratory. The first phase focuses on a low-cost, compact prototype for the 50mm SeeStar S50 telescope, employing a dual-beam configuration with a rotating HWP and a fixed Wollaston prism, establishing a laboratory framework for future upgrades. We detail the optical modeling and key engineering trade-offs. Later phases will scale the instrument and incorporate faster modulators (FLCs/PEMs) and high-sensitivity detectors (PMTs/APDs) to reach the target precision, emphasizing a robust, low-noise polarimetric architecture.

Items.Authors: Daiki Ishi, Yoshitomo Maeda, Manabu Ishida, Asca Miyamoto, Atsuto Matsumura, Tsubasa Uchino
Items.Title: Development of a large-aperture x-ray irradiation system at the ISAS 30-m beam line facility
Items.Abstract: We present a large-aperture x-ray irradiation system developed at the 30-m beam line facility of the Institute of Space and Astronautical Science to enable faster and more flexible calibration of x-ray telescope modules. The system uses an uncollimated, naturally diverging beam from an x-ray generator, reaching 270 mm in diameter at 27 m from the source. Beam baffles suppress scattered x-rays, and a new quadrupole slit assembly defines an illuminated area up to 140 mm × 140 mm within the beam. Beam uniformity measurements with a large-format CMOS detector show spatial variations within 3% for Al and Cu characteristic-line targets. This system supports efficient end-to-end testing of small, lightweight telescope modules for upcoming missions.

Items.Authors: Gwendal Deniel, Jean-Pierre Thermeau, Michel Piat, Marie-Reine N'Sougan, Christophe Chailan, Laurent Grandsire, Alin Ilioni, Patxi Duthil, Rémy Thoër, Jean-Pierre Monchau
Items.Title: Development of a platform dedicated to measuring material properties at cryogenic temperatures: CryoMat
Items.Abstract: The CryoMat project aims to answer a demand in the field of astrophysics, where instruments need to work at cryogenic temperatures to get high sensitivity. A wealth of data on the properties of metallic and plastic materials is now available for temperatures down to 1 K. However, there is still a significant lack of data on thermal, electrical and mechanical properties, particularly for anisotropic materials, and especially composites, across the 1 K – 300 K temperature range, and below 1 K for metallic and plastic materials. CryoMat will aim to fill this gap by developing a platform dedicated to the characterization of materials at cryogenic temperatures, down to sub-Kelvin. This platform, based on the Grands Moulins campus of Université Paris Cité (Paris, France), will be accessible to scientific laboratories and industries. CryoMat will cover three families of physical properties installed in cryostats dedicated to electrical, thermal and mechanical properties.

Items.Authors: Chiara Scandaglia, Matteo Menessini, Runa Briguglio, Marco Xompero, Alberto Riva, Matteo D'Ambrogio
Items.Title: Development of an integrated model of a high order, active segmented mirror for space telescopes
Items.Abstract: The scientific cases of interest for next-generation space telescopes result in challenging requirements for resolution, contrast and wavefront stability, which must be matched with an effective mission risk and cost mitigation. The integration of a deformable primary mirror with contactless actuators may address these needs by enabling active wavefront control, vibration rejection and weight reduction through the use of lighter materials.   The present work aims to provide a parametric integrated model to simulate the effects of the orbital environment on a space telescope equipped with an active segmented primary mirror. The simulator will compute thermal deformations on the support, disturbance propagation to the optics and the wavefront correction to deliver at the focal plane. Through a trade-off study of orbital and system parameters, the goal of the tool is to investigate the attractiveness of the contactless deformable mirror technology in terms of mission cost and performance.

Items.Authors: Kosuke Aizawa, Ryosuke Akizawa, Paolo de Bernardis, Ricardo Tanausú Génova-Santos, Francisco Javier Casas, Shotaro Kawano, Kuniaki Konishi, Luca Lamagna, Asuka Maeda, Enrique Martinez-Gonzalez, Silvia Masi, Tomotake Matsumura, Ilenia Di Nitto, Alessandro Paiella, Guillermo Pascual-Cisneros, Jose Alberto Rubiño-Martín, Haruyuki Sakurai, Ryota Takaku
Items.Title: Development of anti-reflection sub-wavelength structures with laser ablation on sapphires for W-band CMB polarimetry
Items.Abstract: We present optical designs and performances of a sapphire half-wave plate (HWP) for W-band cosmic microwave background (CMB) polarimeters. We designed the HWP with a single layer sapphire with the anti-reflection sub-wavelength structures (SWS) patterned on a sapphire slab using 1030 nm lasers with 4 ps pulse duration and 40 W output power. We fabricated the 20 by 20 SWS array on an A-cut sapphire sample as a prototype demonstration. Based on the fabricated shape, the in-band averaged modulation efficiency and reflection are 93% and < 1%, respectively. The in-band transmittance is larger than 97% considering a loss tangent value of 4\times10^{-4}. We also further optimized the design by taking into account the convergence of the ray into the receiver. We introduce a HWP model to account for the effect of non-parallel rays on the birefringent material including the SWS layer.

Items.Authors: Rekhesh Mohan
Items.Title: Development of CubeSat based UV astronomy payloads at the Indian Institute of Astrophysics: launch opportunities and challenges
Items.Abstract: The space industry is experiencing a paradigm shift globally and within India. There is a widespread interest in CubeSats and nano satellites, leading to a distinct design philosophy for payloads on these platforms. Quite often, the small payloads for astronomy are designed to address specific science cases that are not possible with larger, more sensitive missions. The development of these payloads demands innovation to address the technological challenges. The Small/Space Payloads group at the Indian Institute of Astrophysics (IIA) has been building UV astronomy instruments suited for short-term (1-2 years) missions on CubeSat platforms. In this presentation, I will summarize a few science cases and the UV astronomy payloads being developed to address them. The design of innovative subsystems for these missions will be discussed, and launch opportunities for science payloads in India will also be covered.

Items.Authors: Hidenori Takahashi, Hiroaki Maezawa, Hiroyuki Hashiba, Hidemi Hishino, Masataka Imai
Items.Title: Development of near-infrared scanning Fabry-Perot spectrometer for 3D spectroscopy II: improvements to the final model and practical performances for scientific observations
Items.Abstract: We are developing a Fabry-Perot spectrometer for three-dimensional spectroscopic observation in the near-infrared wavelength range. By achieving the interferometric optical elements variable and combining detector module, it can acquire images at arbitrary wavelengths. Since the spectrometer module must operate under vacuum and low temperature, optical elements (etalon), drive actuators (piezo), and displacement sensor systems (capacitive sensor) optimized for that environment were selected. Its compact shape is optimized for use as a front-end optics of imaging module. Furthermore, a control system is developed that maintains high spectroscopic performance by actively controlling the etalons in real time to constantly maintain the parallelism of the interference gap. The approximate spectroscopic specifications are a resolving power of Res. = 10,000, corresponding to a finesse F = 50 and an interference order of m = 200 at a wavelength of lambda = 2um.

Items.Authors: Sabyasachi Chattopadhyay, Tasheen Naicker, Jonathan Love, Nicolas Erasmus, Hitesh Gajjar, Uhone Mashamba
Items.Title: Development of Second Generation Integral Field Unit for Robert Stobie spectrograph: Slit Mask IFU 300
Items.Abstract: Learning from the development of SMI-200, the new development of second generation SMI-300 would use 248 fibers each with a circular footprint of 1.33 arcsec diameter. The overall IFU will have an extended hexagonal shape of 33 arcsec x 18.6 arcsec. 52.8 mm x 5.8 mm prisms are used the fold the light into fiber inputs while similar prisms are used to feed the spectrograph by folding the fiber output. The prism catheti surfaces were AR coated to less than 1% throughput loss while the hypotenuse were protected Ag coated to better than 95% reflectivity. The object IFU consists of 212 fibers while two sky IFUs would hold 18 fibers each. Precision fabricated metal ferrules position the fibers within 15 micron from an ideal grid to ensure relative exposure time within 5% at any grid point on the object fiber array. In the paper we describe the scientific drivers, fabrication requirements, assembly details and early in-lab characterization results.

Items.Authors: Naoshi Murakami, Jun Nishikawa, Kenta Yoneta, Natsuki Kawauchi, Miho Nagaki, Yuki Hatakeyama, Yosuke Tanaka, Keigo Enya
Items.Title: Development of segmented photonic-crystal phase masks for spectral characterization of exoplanets
Items.Abstract: We are developing coronagraphic segmented phase masks designed for direct detection and spectral characterization of habitable exoplanets. The segmented phase masks can achieve relatively high core throughput with a small inner working angle (IWA). We performed numerical simulations to evaluate the core throughput and the IWA for the segmented phase masks of various orders. Additionally, we simulated observed images for target stars at different distances and spectral types, assuming Earth-like planets in their habitable zones. Development of the phase masks is also underway. We are designing and prototyping broadband phase masks using three-layer photonic crystals optimized for the visible and near-infrared (NIR) regimes. The fabricated masks are evaluated in the laboratory, mainly in the visible at present and in the NIR in future work. In this presentation, we report recent activities in our ongoing simulations and phase-mask development efforts.

Items.Authors: Hiroshi Matsuo, Hajime Ezawa, T. Koseki, S. Inoue, T. Seino
Items.Title: Development of terahertz intensity interferometry for very high angular resolution studies
Items.Abstract: To realize high angular resolution in far-infrared (FIR) and terahertz (THz) range, imaging capability of intensity interferometry is studied. Using high sensitivity SIS photon detectors and cryogenic readout electronics operational at 0.8 K, we have realized fast intensity measurement system for intensity correlation measurements. We have evaluated that the system sensitivity is enough to measure delay time within 1 ps between two beams using 600 GHz SIS photon detectors and GaAs FETs observing high temperature blackbody. Imaging capability based on the laboratory experiment will be discussed. We are planning astronomical demonstrations of THz intensity interferometry from Dome-Fuji, Antarctica, using two 30-cm telescopes. Prospects of space-borne FIR intensity interferometry and their observational capability will be discussed.

Items.Authors: Austin R. Stover, Juliang Li, Peter Sharpe, Morgana Iacocca, Erin Healy, Audrey Scott, Jessica Zebrowski, Jeffrey McMahon
Items.Title: Development of the High-density Vertical Integral Spectrometer (HI-VIS) focal plane, a densely packed spectrometer array architecture for highly sensitive line intensity mapping surveys
Items.Abstract: HI-VIS, the High-density Vertical Integrated Spectrometer, is a mm-wave integral field unit architecture for intensity mapping with a densely packed focal plane. Such a focal plane enables the deployment of hundreds of spectrometers on existing and future telescopes which is needed to achieve the required sensitivities for Line Intensity Mapping surveys. HI-VIS orients on-chip spectrometers parallel to incident light, which increases detector density by a factor of 25 and enables spectral surveys of weak signals in previously unexplored redshift regimes. HI-VIS comprises an array of feedhorn antennas coupled to on-chip filter-bank spectrometers by an in-line waveguide-to-on-chip transition, with readout by microwave kinetic inductance detectors. To form the transition, a chip is bump-bonded to a 3D-printed and metallized ceramic waveguide structure. We present the measured performance of a prototype of this transition in the 85–170 GHz band and the status of the development of HI-VIS.

Items.Authors: I. Di Nitto, P. de Bernardis, F. Cacciotti, A. Coppolecchia, L. Lamagna, S. Masi, A. Paiella, G. Pettinari, F. Piacentini, G. Pisano, A. Volpe, K. Aizawa, R. Akizawa, M. Bouzit, D. Carroll, F. J. Casas, L. Castelló Gomar, J. J. Diaz Garcia, R. T. Génova-Santos, H. L. Hernandez, R. J. Hoyland, E. de la Hoz Lopez-Collado, A. Marcos-Caballero, E. Martínez-González, T. Matsumura, A. B. Nuñez-Chico, G. Pascual-Cisneros, A. Perez de Taoro, J. A. Rubiño-Martín, A. Vega, A. Zamora Jimenez
Items.Title: Development of the optical coupling system for the QUIJOTE 90GHz instrument
Items.Abstract: In this contribution, we present the development of a W-band camera for the QUIJOTE experiment based on a polarization-sensitive KID array, extending its coverage from 10–40 GHz to the W-band. This band offers an optimal balance between atmospheric emission, galactic foregrounds, and CMB signal. Due to stringent space constraint, reimaging optics cannot be used, so detectors are placed directly at the focal plane and coupled through a 50 K feedhorn array connected to circular waveguides guiding radiation to the sub-K stage. Waveguide single-mode operation preserves polarization purity, while flares and chokes reduce power leakage and cross-talk. A band-pass filter between the vacuum window and the 50 K stage and in-guide low-pass filters protect KIDs from excessive radiative load. The feedhorn design minimizes aperture while keeping low sidelobes. HFSS-simulated beam patterns were integrated into GRAP to assess spillover, cross-polarization, and symmetry for system optimization.

Items.Authors: Massinissa Hadjara, Volodymyr Akhmetov, Jean-Eudes Arlot, Jennifer Lynn Bartlett, Beatrice Bucciarelli, Thom R. Burns, Jaime Carrillo, Chenzhou Cui, Shuhrat Ehgamberdiev, Ilgmars Eglitis, Silvia Galleti, Salvo Guglielmino, Daniel Hestroffer, Rene Hudec, Peter Kroll, Elizabeth Kruesi, Stephen Levine, Shanna Li, Wangu Li, Jun Lin, Verónica Lencinas, Mingyang Ma, Vicente Maldonado, Andrea Mejías, Rene A. Mendez, Alessandro Omizzolo, Wayne Osborn, Sibilla Perina, Anton Pomazan, Bo Qiu, Quanfeng Xu, Maryam Raouph, Vincent Robert, Takashi Sakurai, Brad Schaefer, Andreas Schrimpf, Zhengjun Shang, Chunhui J. Shi, Alessandro Spagna, Christiaan Sterken, Zhenghong Tang, Gabriele Umbriaco, Liangliang Wang, Tianyi Wang, Kenshi Yanagisawa, Dan Yan, Jing Yang, Meiting Yang, Haibo Yuan, Yong Yu, Qudratillo Yuldoshev, Tauseef A. Zafar, Jianhai Zhao, Yongheng Zhao, Wenwen Zuo
Items.Title: Digitizing astronomical plates around the world: past, present, and future strategies
Items.Abstract: The digitization of astronomical plates is critical for preserving centuries of astronomical observations. This poster presents the efforts of the PDPP-IAU Working Group to advance the digitization of historical plates through international initiatives. We summarize the contributions of major scanning facilities: Shanghai Astronomical Observatory (SHAO), DASCH, the Royal Observatory of Belgium, and the NAROO center at Paris Observatory in Meudon. Key public databases are also highlighted: QLPER (China), APPLAUSE (Germany), and APDA-PARI at Pisgah Astronomical Research Institute (USA). We review the current state of plate archives worldwide, stressing their continued scientific value and the urgency of preservation. Future strategies, technological improvements, and enhanced collaborations are discussed to ensure global safeguarding of these irreplaceable records. This work underscores the importance of protecting our astronomical heritage for future research and outreach.

Items.Authors: H. Hope Head, David Morris, Nuria Wright-Garba, Francisco Salinas, Anthony Santini, Andres Parraguez, Alexandra Tritschler, David Boboltz
Items.Title: DKIST science operations specialists’ skills training program implementation
Items.Abstract: Building upon our work in developing a knowledge training program presented at SPIE 2024, the Science Operations Specialists at the National Science Foundation’s Daniel K. Inouye Solar Telescope further extended our in-house training program for new hires to incorporate a new element. Specifically, we included training to enhance competency with procedures required for operational tasks, thus increasing overall proficiency in operations. The primary objectives of this specialized skills training program were to enhance the efficiency and speed of the training process, establish a systematic approach for defining proficiency with the operational systems and tools, and enable supervisors to monitor and document the completion of training milestones. To support this initiative, the team used Confluence, JIRA, ClassMarker and Google Sheets to develop all facets of the Skills Training Program, including a framework for tracking and managing the stages of the training program’s development.

Items.Authors: Ohgan Kim, Ho-Soon Yang
Items.Title: Dual-path phase unwrapping algorithm based on geodesic curvature for interferometric fringe analysis
Items.Abstract: We propose a fast and noise-resistant dual-path phase unwrapping algorithm based on geodesic curvature for interferometric fringe analysis. The method resolves 2π-modulo inconsistencies by mapping wrapped phase data onto a cylindrical surface, where each 1-D profile forms a helical curve whose azimuthal angle variation directly represents the true phase gradient. Extending this concept to 2-D, two independent unwrapping paths—row-wise and column-wise—are combined to suppress local errors and reduce the influence of undersampled regions. Experiments using synthetic data and real interferometer measurements show that the proposed algorithm matches the speed of MATLAB’s UNWRAP function while improving accuracy near boundaries. It also maintains noise resistance comparable to PUMA and Goldstein methods up to an SNR of 6 dB. Owing to its simplicity, high speed, and robustness, the algorithm is well suited for real-time optical metrology and related phase-retrieval applications.

Items.Authors: Peter P. Pedersen, Clark E. Baker, Karolina Dziewiecka, Mathias Beck, Didier Queloz
Items.Title: DUET: design of a simultaneous InGaAs–CCD split-beam imager for ultra-cool dwarf exoplanet transit survey
Items.Abstract: We present the design of DUET, a dual-channel imager being built for the SPECULOOS-Southern Observatory (SSO) to detect and characterise transiting terrestrial exoplanets orbiting ultra-cool dwarfs. A dichroic beamsplitter at 955 nm directs visible light to a deeply-depleted silicon CCD and near-infrared light to a CMOS-based InGaAs detector, enabling fully simultaneous photometry with bandpasses from 0.4 to 1.7 microns. The near-infrared filters have been chosen to suppress sensitivity to atmospheric precipitable water vapour (PWV) variability, a dominant source of correlated noise in ground-based infrared photometry of cool stars. We describe the optical and mechanical architecture, the dichroic and filter selection, the choice of detectors, and the control system.

Items.Authors: Rustam Balafendiev, Miranda Eiben, Jón E. Gudmundsson
Items.Title: Effects of manufacturing tolerances on the performance of metamaterial microwave anti-reflection coatings
Items.Abstract: Metamaterial anti-reflection coatings (ARC) are used in a variety of applications: lenses, filters, absorbers and so on. Typically, the design of a given ARC is done within an infinite medium approximation, which assumes that every unit cell on the interface is identical. However, in reality, the geometry of a given ARC usually has some degree of variability, be it due to the shape of the surface inherent to the application or manufacturing tolerances. This variation may alter the performance of the optical element in unanticipated ways, by creating additional scattering, enabling diffractive maxima that would normally be absent and changing the transparency of the ARC as a function of frequency. In this work we utilize full-wave modelling of finite samples of plastic with a metamaterial ARC on both of their interfaces. By adding a degree of randomness to the ARC geometry we attempt to characterise the extent to which a given variation affects the expected performance of an ARC.

Items.Authors: Matteo D'Ambrogio, Davide Greggio, Cédric Taïssir Héritier, Mary Angelie Alagao, Mohamed Y. Bournane, Elena Carolo, Alessandro Ballone, Silvio Di Rosa, Ivan Di Antonio, Eduard Muslimov, Aurelie Magniez, Matteo Menessini, Pietro Ferraiuolo
Items.Title: EKARUS at Asiago Observatory: optomechanical design and AIT procedures of the visible stage
Items.Abstract: EKARUS is the successor of the PAPYRUS bench, developed collaboratively by ONERA/LAM and INAF, and will be installed in the Coudé room of the Copernico telescope at Asiago. It is a SCAO facility enabling on-sky testing of different wavefront sensors and adaptive optics techniques. We present the optomechanical design of its first stage operating in the visible, which integrates a deformable mirror, a fast tip-tilt mirror, and a pyramid wavefront sensor, along with two visitor WFSs ports and a science camera providing a 1 arcmin FoV. The design balances optical performance, mechanical constraints, and available space. We also outline considerations for assembly, integration, and testing to ensure system alignment and stability. EKARUS's assembly, integration, and testing will begin in May 2026. The instrument will have its first light in September 2026. Key alignment procedures include collimation, beam centering, fine Tip-Tilt adjustments, and final performance measurements.

Items.Authors: Himadri Saha, Netty Honingh, Jonathan Clarke, Kian Syaifoel, Matthias Justen, Felix Münning, Yoko Okada, Jochem Baselmans, Dominik A. Riechers
Items.Title: Electromagnetic design and modelling of efficient integrated filterbanks towards a spectroscopic focal plane array for CCAT/FYST
Items.Abstract: A spectroscopic focal plane array based on on-chip Integrated Filterbank Spectrometers (IFBSs) is a promising way for [CII] Line Intensity Mapping with sub-mm facilities such as CCAT/FYST. We present and compare the design and modelling of a R ~ 100 IFBS device with three suitable filter structures for the filterbank section. We consider the trade-offs of astronomical forecasts and design complexity. We present the filterbank synthesis with higher order bandpass filters, showing reduced crosstalk and near-unity transmission. We introduce a numerical model for the filterbank spectral transmission validate with an electromagnetic simulation for the three filter types. Finally, we explore how the reduced crosstalk improves the expected recovery of redshifted [CII] line power spectrum.

Items.Authors: Davide Savio, Ernesto Oliva, Alen Khanbekyan, Anna Brucalassi, Andrea Tozzi
Items.Title: Empirical characterization and modelling of modal noise in multimode fibres for next-generation high-resolution spectrographs
Items.Abstract: Modal noise is a major limitation in multimode fibres used for high-resolution astronomical spectroscopy, introducing non-averaging interference patterns that degrade signal-to-noise ratio and bias wavelength calibration. We present a comprehensive laboratory study using a dedicated setup that reproduces realistic fibre-feeding conditions. High-resolution spectra and near-/far-field images were acquired for multiple fibre geometries, scrambling schemes, and illumination regimes, allowing us to identify how mode excitation, under-filling, mechanical perturbations, and fibre shape influence modal noise power. Fourier analysis reveals a power-law behaviour and shows how octagonal fibres and double scramblers shift power toward higher spectral frequencies. Based on these results, we developed an empirical model that replicates the observed behaviour and provides a predictive tool to guide hardware mitigation and design choices for next-generation spectrographs.

Items.Authors: Matt Lyons, Pete Hargrave, Ian Veenendaal, Rashmi Sudiwala, Lottie Braithewaite, Giorgio Savini, Alexey Shitvov, Jin Zhang, Jon E. Gudmundsson
Items.Title: End-to-end precision characterisation of broadband antireflection-coated mm-wave components
Items.Abstract: Future sub-millimetre optical systems require low-loss, low-reflectance, broadband anti-reflection (AR) coatings, for which interspersed polymer layers with matched refractive indices are a proven option. However, hot-press bonding can change refractive index and deform the optic substrate, degrading lens performance. We address this by annealing the substrate before machining, relieving internal stresses and stabilizing optical properties so the AR-coating process does not distort the lens. We investigate cast polypropylene (CPP) and porous PTFE (pPTFE) as coating materials for UHMWPE optics and identify an optimal annealing cycle enabling reliable fabrication and characterization. Using spectroscopy and an MCMC-based transfer-matrix model, we extract refractive index and loss from 60–900 GHz. These measurements inform optimized 3- and 5-layer AR-coating designs validated on 70 mm pucks and demonstrated on a full-size two-lens system operating over 166–448 GHz.

Items.Authors: Michael Weber
Items.Title: Environment aware wavelength calibration of thermally stabilized echelle spectrographs
Items.Abstract: Thermally controlled echelle spectrograph are on short (one night) timescales limited in stability by atmospheric pressure variations which lead to variations in the refractive index of air. With STELLA/SES we record about 10 HCL spectra over the course of the night, and we noticed that the calibration accuracy is worse if the atmospheric pressure variation has a turning point between two calibrations. We tried to mitigate this by introducing the pressure as additional parameter in the calibration procedure, which only worked in perfect conditions.  Recently we derived a scheme where the wavelengths of observations and of the calibration line positions are treated at current conditions, and then transformed to vacuum using Ciddor's equation. This also works during bad observing conditions (partial nights, broken HCL lamp) and has the added bonus of providing a quantitative quality measure of the wavelength calibration quality.

Items.Authors: Élodie Choquet, Lisa Altinier, Nicolás Godoy, Alexis Lau, Sophie Noiret, Anton Neisius, Arthur Vigan
Items.Title: ESCAPE project: investigating observing strategies and post-processing methods for future high-contrast imaging space missions
Items.Abstract: The search for biosignatures in potentially habitable exoplanets is one of the major astrophysics’ drivers for the coming decades. It is the prime science case of HWO, a large space telescope that will be equipped with state-of-the art capabilities to directly characterize Earth-like planets in the 2040s. Ahead of this, the Roman Space Telescope will demonstrate critical technologies to reach 1e-8 contrast limits, using wavefront control and optimized coronagraphs for the first time in space.   Given the stringent constraints on wavefront stability required to achieve these unprecedented contrast levels, new observing strategies and data post-processing techniques need to be developed to optimize detection capabilities with these missions.   Here, we introduce the ESCAPE project, which explore new observing strategies that make use of the deformable mirrors to systematically sample wavefront variations during reference star observations to optimize the detection limits at postprocessing.

Items.Authors: Fernando Merlos-García, Jorge Quintero Nehrkorn, Ángela Hernández-Delgado, Josué Barrera Martín, José Antonio Rodríguez Losada, Javier León-Gil, Miguel Núñez Cagigal, Manuel Collados, Mary Barreto Cabrera, Héctor Socas-Navarro
Items.Title: EST control system: how architecture design can reduce the impact of obsolescence
Items.Abstract: The European Solar Telescope (EST) will become ones of the best solar telescope and is intended to be fully operational for about 50 years. The design of the control system architecture aims, among others, to reduce the impact of obsolescence, remaining as independent as possible from specific technologies, as well as increase resource optimization.

Items.Authors: A. Mazzoli, C. Dandumont, A. Besse, B. Borguet, J. Bouwmeester, D. Defrère, I. Khan, R. Laugier, J. Loicq, V. Moreau, P. Piron, R. Saathof, I. Sigusch, P. Hallibert, D. Alaluf, Luca Schifano, T. Rank-Lueftinger
Items.Title: Exoplanet explorer: optical design of a single spacecraft nulling interferometer
Items.Abstract: The optical design layout of a single spacecraft nulling interferometer is presented here as part of a study initiated by ESA to explore the design parameters and performance of an interferometric concept based on a single spacecraft with multiple sub-apertures.Launch constraints drive the ray-traced model to cover the entire optical chain, from the telescope entrance to the null output after the recombination scheme. A trade-off among several telescope architectures led to the choice of a compact two-mirror solution consisting of a four 2.5m diameter telescopes arranged in a linear configuration with an extended baseline.Optical performance at the null output is evaluated, confirming compatibility with starlight suppression targets and establishing the key figures of merit for the interferometer. This work represents the first integrated optical design of the mission concept, laying the groundwork for future iterations that include mechanical, thermal, and control aspects.

Items.Authors: Osamu Tajima
Items.Title: Experimental concepts for probing wavy dark matter using coherent detection techniques for CMB observations
Items.Abstract: Direct detection of dark matter remains a major challenge, as its mass and non-gravitational interactions are still unknown despite strong astronomical evidence. Wavy dark matter candidates, such as axions and dark photons, motivate searches across wide mass ranges. Radio-astronomy-based techniques are promising; recent experiments like DOSUE-RR have explored the 100 μeV region using 24-GHz conversion searches. Current experiments constrain only mass and coupling, leaving polarization and arrival direction unprobed. Coherent detection, widely used in CMB measurements, can access these properties thanks to the long coherence length of wavy dark matter. This presentation introduces experimental concepts that apply coherent detection to such searches.

Items.Authors: Shoken Myozen, Kosuke Aizawa, Ryosuke Akizawa, Ludovico Bizzarri, Thomas Essinger-Hileman, Tommaso Ghigna, Shotaro Kawano, Kuniaki Konishi, Asuka Maeda, Tomotake Matsumura, Noemi Mezzanzanica, Haruyuki Sakurai, Ryota Takaku, Mario Zannoni
Items.Title: Exploration of simplified W-band feedhorn design and fabrication
Items.Abstract: We present on the development of a simplified design and fabrication approach for a W-band feedhorn for measurements of cosmic microwave background (CMB) polarization. The next generation CMB observations need scales of order up to 1,000,000 for ground-based telescopes. Feedhorns, optical coupling elements, must be produced in quantities of at least one quarter of the total detector count. The fabrication of the multi-array feedhorn has been one of the bottlenecks in the development step. We explore ways to simplify the feedhorn fabrication. We approximated the profile to be a straight line within one segment of which the feedhorn is divided into five. The simulations show the segmented design achieves 22.05 dB gain at 90 GHz and 30% bandwidth around 90 GHz, which is comparable to that of the profiled feedhorn. We report the design results. We also report the status of the further explorations using multi-layer feedhorn approaches using laser machining.

Items.Authors: Zongliang Xie
Items.Title: Extended object image-based piston sensing
Items.Abstract: JWST’s success has motivated interest in large-aperture segmented telescopes for Earth observation, offering the potential for unprecedented ground resolution. A key challenge, however, is phasing such systems directly from remote sensing images. Here we report a remote sensing image-based optical differential piston sensing approach, capable of detecting large optical path length differences, i.e. coarse phasing. Initially the features respond to the pistons of each non-reference segment are extracted through both continuous piston modulation and differential operation. Then the Gaussian fitting is performed to identify the optimal response, and the coarse piston inversion can be realized. With this strategy, large piston errors can be corrected to within one wavelength using remote sensing images, free from constraints on the number of segments. The proposed method may contribute to the development of the extremely large Earth observation systems with hundreds of segments.

Items.Authors: P. Ashworth, P. S. Barry, C. S. Benson, K. Dibert, H. Gordon-Moys, P. Hunyor, K. S. Karkare, I. Morris, A. Tan
Items.Title: Fabrication of silicon etched vacuum waveguides for a superconducting millimeter-wave spectrometer
Items.Abstract: We present a prototype device using micromachined silicon waveguides, coated with superconducting niobium. A simple channelising filter-bank composed of single pole iris-coupled cavity resonators disperses the incident light, with each spectral channel coupled to an in-plane waveguide that enables efficient, straightforward detector integration. Implementing detailed electromagnetic simulations, we report the design, optimisation, and fabrication of a small-scale prototype R = 500 waveguide spectrometer based on the standard WR3 geometry operating across the 1 mm (220–310 GHz) atmospheric window.

Items.Authors: Binbin Xiang, Shike Mo, XueTong Yang, Wei Wang, Longfei Niu
Items.Title: Fault diagnosis technique for radio telescope antenna drive reducer gears based on the fused model
Items.Abstract: Low-speed operation of antenna drive reducer gears suffers from reduced SNR, obscuring fault features under noise interference where traditional methods fail. This study proposes an RBMO-optimized SVMD-MCKD-CNN-LSTM fusion model (RSM-CL) for fault diagnosis. RBMO-optimized SVMD-MCKD first enhances raw signals via noise reduction and feature amplification. Subsequently, CNN extracts localized spatial features while LSTM captures temporal dependencies for deep fault characterization. Experimental validation demonstrates the model achieves >97% average classification accuracy, outperforming conventional single-decomposition/single-model approaches in both diagnostic precision and computational efficiency (reduced processing time). This framework establishes a novel solution for low-speed reducer gear fault diagnosis.

Items.Authors: Luke M. Schmidt, Hudson Malone, Noah Siebersma, Erika Cook, Jennifer L. Marshall, Darren L. DePoy, Ryan J. Oelkers, Silvana Delgado Andrade, Enrique Gonzalez Vega, Shravan Menon, Chelsea Taylor, Lars Walker
Items.Title: Fiber optic characterization for unprecedented sky subtraction (FOCUSS)
Items.Abstract: Future massively multiplexed astronomical spectroscopic surveys will require accurate and repeatable removal of  the sky background. The Fiber Optic Characterization for Unprecedented Sky Subtraction (FOCUSS) project  aims to automate the characterization of fiber optic cables in order to determine their throughput efficiency  and focal ratio degradation (FRD). The laboratory setup is useful for fiber optic selection, fiber optic assembly  verification, and potentially inform the development of telescope facility calibration systems. The throughput  efficiency measures the fiber transmission as a function of wavelength, while the FRD test measures the angular  spread of light exiting the test fiber as a function of incident angle. FOCUSS operates between 350-1000 nm and  uses the Python programming language for data collection, reduction, and analysis.

Items.Authors: Valentina Viotto, Alessandro Ballone, Davide Greggio, Luca Marafatto, Carmelo Arcidiacono, Andrea Baruffolo, Maria Bergomi, Elena Carolo, Simonetta Chinellato, Simone Di Filippo, Marco Dima, Jacopo Farinato, Demetrio Magrin, Lorenzo Merli, Roberto Ragazzoni, Oleksandra Rebrysh, Kalyan Kumar Radhakrishnan Santhakumari, Daniele Vassallo, David Barr, Sylvain Cetre, Gabriele Umbriaco
Items.Title: Final design of the MATTO test bench
Items.Abstract: The MATTO test bench, under development at INAF-OAPD, is a multi-purpose wide-field AO test facility, whose opto-mechanical design is aimed at simulating existing or future MCAO systems configurations with test or validation purposes. It will allow exploring a wide range of WFSs and sources combinations, thanks to the modularity of its design. It includes a reference source module, which simulates the atmospheric behaviour on natural and laser guide stars, a telescope simulator module, a MCAO correction module, allowing to mimic a number of optical configurations in which three DMs can be independently conjugated at various distances, and a sensing module, which allows to replicate the main properties of different types of WFSs. The DAO4MATTO Real-Time Control system, based on the DAO software solution, will provide MCAO loop control, keeping the system’s modular approach, for all possible configurations.
